Hydrogen ions are formed when aerobic oxidation of fats supplies most of the ATP. Oxidising fats generates NADH and FADH₂, and the resulting H⁺ is pumped across the mitochondrial membrane and released in the process. Phosphocreatine breakdown consumes H⁺ (PCr + ADP + H⁺ → Cr + ATP), so it doesn't fit. My earlier general answer about acids releasing protons was off-target for this question. I'm choosing between only the two options in the team note, because I can't see the original question's options.
